title: WaterPaths-WSS: multi-subsystem WaterPaths for the Federal District of Brazil (v1.0.0)
description:
WaterPaths-WSS is a modified version of WaterPaths (Trindade et al., 2020), an open-source C++ stochastic simulation and many-objective optimization framework for regional water-supply portfolio and infrastructure planning under deep uncertainty. It adds an explicit Water Supply System (WSS) layer so that a single utility can operate several hydraulically distinct subsystems, a configuration common in large utilities that the original framework could only represent as separate, independent utilities.

The model is configured for CAESB, the water utility of the Federal District of Brazil, with two subsystems: Descoberto (Descoberto Reservoir and Corumbá IV) and Torto/Santa Maria (Santa Maria/Torto Reservoir, the Bananal and Torto intakes, and emergency supply from Lake Paranoá). The CAESB problem builds on Araújo et al. (2024; doi:10.5281/zenodo.8221350). The author of this record did not develop WaterPaths or the original CAESB model; this release documents and distributes the modifications.

Main modifications

  • Multi-subsystem architecture: a new WaterSupplySystems class. Each WSS has its own demands, tariffs, demand classes, source-to-WTP mapping, wastewater returns, risk-of-failure (ROF) state, infrastructure construction order and triggers, and financial accounting. The parent utility pools debt service and contingency funds and coordinates shared infrastructure.
  • Per-WSS ROF: the continuity models and pre-computed ROF tables are computed per subsystem.
  • Drought instruments at subsystem level: three-stage restrictions with tariff surcharges; bilateral transfers between subsystems with a sender demand-protection factor; and a new ROF-triggered emergency transfer from Lake Paranoá whose capacity grows with Paranoá WTP expansions and which gates their construction.
  • New objectives: per-subsystem reliability, affordability index (water bill ÷ household income) and optional failure severity, with eight experiment modes (minimax, average, per-subsystem, single-subsystem, penalty-based and disparity/equity-gap formulations).
  • Outputs and robustness: per-WSS time series, pathways and annual reliability outputs; thread-safe per-realization copies; handling of failed Borg evaluations; portable CLI; CMake build. 22 decision variables, up to 7 objectives.

Requirements: C++14 with OpenMP and MPI; optimization also requires Borg MOEA (not included; http://borgmoea.org). Input data and ROF tables: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23492993.
